---
title: "FSPP Research Workbench"
---

This website is the top-level publication surface for the **FSPP Research Workbench**. It collects independently rendered subsites built from versioned workbench records, schemas, codebooks, run manifests, and generated research artifacts.

Canonical evidence remains in the repository's project data and research files. The website is a rendered snapshot for review, publication, and audit.

## Workbench Status

| Area | Status |
|---|---|
| Repository | Public GitHub repository configured on `master` with pull-request validation. |
| Publication | Top-level Quarto site plus independently configured Engineering and Sacrificial Debt subsites. |
| Runtime | Python 3.14, Node.js 24 LTS, uv-managed virtual environment, Quarto publication build. |
| Validation | Ruff, pytest, schema checks, canonical-data validation, and site rendering are active gates. |
| Research posture | Manual-first pilot infrastructure; no automated extraction or released findings. |

## Research Projects

### [Sacrificial Debt](projects/sacrificial-debt/)

Sacrificial Debt is the first native project in the Workbench. It tests when perceived exemption from collective sacrifice can become an attributed political debt and under what additional conditions that debt becomes essentialized, non-dischargeable, or coercively collected.

| Field | Current State |
|---|---|
| Milestone status | Milestone 1 pilot infrastructure is ready for closeout review. |
| Pilot scope | Germany-first manual pilot, with contrast cases deferred. |
| Evidence state | One project-owner reviewed Segall 1922 calibration packet is rendered for audit. |
| Claim state | No released findings or promoted Sacrificial Debt claims. |
| Data authority | Canonical JSONL, codebook, corpus, and research files remain authoritative. |
| Next research need | More rights-reviewed source captures, manually reviewed propositions, reliability/adjudication workflow, and evidence chains. |

## Engineering

### [Workbench Engineering](engineering/)

The Engineering subsite documents the operational parts of the Workbench: runtime requirements, validation gates, publication builds, GitHub workflow, source/data boundaries, and the separation between shared infrastructure and project-specific research theory.

| Area | Current State |
|---|---|
| Runtime environment | Project-local `.venv/` managed by `uv`, with checked-in version expectations. |
| CI and validation | GitHub Actions runs lint, tests, schema freshness, and data validation on pull requests. |
| Publication model | Quarto renders the Workbench home and each subsite independently for GitHub Pages. |
| Agent workflow | `AGENTS.md` and the SDLC skill define branch, PR, review, merge, and closeout expectations for Codex first and Claude as backup. |

::: {.callout-note}
Each subsite owns its own Quarto configuration, navigation, styling, and content. Additional projects, such as Lincoln Metaphor Analysis and Sacrifice Law, can be added as sibling subsites under `publication/projects/` when their workbench adapters or native project modules are ready.
:::
